text: We will need to serve the packets that are in each queue a little bit differently, one from the other. So now you can actually say, well, but you told us that actually they were behaving as in the previous case. There was no difference. Now you are saying that they behave a little bit differently. Why? What is going on? Well, the rules that each server of these queues follows are exactly the same as before. So we don't need to really learn new things. There are just a few details that we will have in mind. In principle, they follow exactly the same rules. What changes is the value of the mark parameters, of the parameters that they use to apply the rules. For example, rule number one: if you want to transmit a data packet, you have to sense the channel for beeps, right? Unless it's an ACK. In that case, it's a SIFS or we are within a dialogue, then SIFS. But otherwise, if you want to transmit a new data packet, you have to sense the channel for beeps. Okay, so the sensing time of this high priority queue will be indeed beeps. But this other queue that has got lower priority traffic will have a sensing time a little bit more than beeps. And this queue.
